items: Home is dressed with its own set: lantern posts, path lights, flower pots, mushroom rings and stepping stones round the dancefloor's clearing, a fairy-lit branch arch over each path, and a speaker stack, crates and a signpost by the treehouse

Wild areas grow: every area starts with one baby and one adult, and each wave every area the party hasn't reached gains another creature, a baby, young or adult. So the longer an area stays wild, the bigger the army that marches when its wave comes, and old wild areas get dangerous to cross on foot. Newcomers turn up out of sight, never popping in
Debug overlay (~): a power meter, your party's fighting strength (on your leash and parked) against each siege's and all the marchers together
A playtest log: every 10 s of play it notes your party, the waves and the sieges on this browser; press L (or open the game with ?playtest=download) to save it as a file to send
Wild creatures go for you as soon as you land in their area (not just when you're close); they still give up when you rise, or once you've left their area and are well away
The creature you're chatting to won't attack you while you talk (its friends still will)
Creatures enraged by a wave (attacking a soundsystem) have angry red eyes and can't be invited
Beaten creatures no longer vanish: they run off, out of the forest, and are gone for good (yours too: a beaten party animal runs away off its leash)
Creatures notice you from further away: they turn to look at you, curious babies come up to you and shy ones keep their distance; fights pick up from further off too

Creatures fight in their own ways: wolves spread out to surround you, hares dart in and back out, boars charge in a straight line (sidestep!), bats swarm without piling up, ravens line up and shoot on the beat, spiders lie still until you come close
New attacks: owls lob shots that land where you were standing (a ring shows where; move out of it), salamanders and spiders burn you with beams
A test arena for creature fights: add ?arena=wolf*4,raven*3 to the link (your side first, @2 for adults); J starts it again

Creatures have traits you can see, as marks by their health bars: fliers (blue) take half from melee, armoured ones (grey square) take a third from shots, lobs and beams but get knocked over and stunned by knockback, swarms (violet) take double from area attacks, heavy ones (brown square) won't be knocked back
A hit that's strong against its target bursts gold with "!!"; one it resists goes "tink"
Moles burrow: a mound of earth races over the ground at you (nothing can hit it) and the mole bursts up under you
Toads leap at you in an arc and slam down: a ring shows where they'll land
Bats screech all round themselves (a ring shows its reach), spiders spit webs (an adult's slows you), beetles plod in slowly but are hard to stop

Wild legends fight with big, slow, telegraphed moves in a pattern: a ground slam (a ring shows its reach), a nova of shots all round (spokes show it coming), and a charge (it backs off, then thunders down a lane you can see)
At half health a wild legend roars (a red burst, the screen shakes) into its second phase: faster, with a beam it spins all the way round (a circle shows its reach), and a red aura

Ley lines: a glowing chain runs through the runestones in the order the waves will wake them, from the last wave's stone on through the next few, each link fainter than the one before. They wander along the valleys between the stones, a shimmer flows along them toward the later stone, and over the treetops they rise above the canopy so you can steer by them (?ley=0 hides them)
Boosting over the hills is smooth again: no more hitches as new ground streams in ahead of you
Wide undergrowth and thickets no longer float at their downhill end on steep slopes

The music takes its mood from Ed's two favourite references: dreamy, ethereal choirs and sung notes over the forest, then harder, darker waves with distorted industrial drums, metal clanks, a gritty bass and string stabs, then breakbeats; the bubblegum and chiptune waves have made way (a flash of chiptune still sparkles in the frenzy)

The music sounds bigger and clearer: crisp 808-style hats, a punchier kick with a click, wide detuned supersaw leads, breathing pads, a darker, deeper reverb, and everything rebalanced so the drums, bass, chords and melodies each have their own space
A big glowing number over every rune stone: the wave that will wake it (dimmed once the party's there)
Every area now has its own legend, asleep for centuries: half sunk into the ground and grown over with moss, easy to mistake for a mound. Walking by won't wake it
When the party reaches its area, the legend heaves up out of the ground, angry, and guards its area: it goes for you, your animals and that area's soundsystem, but never leaves its area
Beat a legend and it sinks back to sleep for good. Home's legend is happy and on your side from the start; press O to make the nearest legend happy (a stand-in until quests): its buff turns on
Party animals now evolve only up to adult: legends are the areas' own

A happy legend guards its area for you: it takes on sieges marching through or on its soundsystem with its big moves, heals between fights, and if it's beaten it sinks back to sleep (its buff gone). See it in the arena: ?arena=home,wolf*6@2!
Flagstones round the dancefloor out past its speakers: rings of mossy old stone where there was bare grass
